quote.quote: This product was discussed at an Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee meeting on September 14, 2011.
A meeting of the Oncology Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) was held on September 14, 2011 to discuss the deferiprone application.

recommendation.text: The committee voted 10 (yes) to 2 (no) that the available clinical data demonstrate a favorable risk-benefit profile for deferiprone.

quote.quote: The Committee voted 10 (yes) to 2 (no) that the available clinical data demonstrate a favorable risk-benefit profile for deferiprone.

linkages.concern: The central question put to ODAC was whether the 20% reduction in serum ferritin (a surrogate endpoint) was an appropriate primary endpoint to support approval.
linkages.change: The 20% serum ferritin endpoint was accepted as the basis for accelerated approval, with ODAC's supporting vote cited as corroboration that the chosen degree of improvement was appropriate.

concern_quote.quote: The choice of the primary endpoint, 20% reduction in baseline serum ferritin over a year, was discussed at the September 14, 2011 Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting.

change_quote.quote: A 20% decrease in serum ferritin is an appropriate degree of improvement for use in defining the primary endpoint, according to a consensus opinion among investigators and as agreed by ODAC by their supporting vote recommending approval (10 to 2).

linkages.concern: Some ODAC members, while voting in favor of approval, emphasized the importance of additional (confirmatory) studies.
linkages.change: The accelerated (Subpart H) approval required the applicant to conduct postapproval studies to verify and describe clinical benefit.

concern_quote.quote: Some ODAC members in favor of approval while emphasizing the importance of additional studies, as required under our accelerated approval framework.

change_quote.quote: the applicant is required to conduct postapproval studies to verify and describe clinical benefit in patients.

summary: An Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) meeting was held September 14, 2011 for deferiprone (Ferriprox), and the committee voted 10-2 that the clinical data showed a favorable risk-benefit profile in patients inadequately treated by current chelation. The review documents explicitly cite ODAC's supporting vote as corroborating acceptance of the 20% serum ferritin reduction as the primary surrogate endpoint for accelerated approval; ODAC was supportive rather than a source of mandated label changes. The agranulocytosis boxed warning and the required postapproval studies are attributed in the reviews to the drug's safety profile and the Subpart H accelerated-approval framework, not explicitly to ODAC concerns.
